label: Era III begins
why: Era III begins: the Spanish and Ottoman empires at their height, Akbar's Mughal Empire, Abbas's Safavid revival, and Japan on the eve of Sekigahara.

realms.name: Spanish Monarchy (Crown of Castile)
realms.note: Composite monarchy of Castile, Aragon, Portugal, Italian and Burgundian dominions; Indies governed through the viceroyalties of New Spain and Peru. Court moves to Valladolid in 1601.

realms.name: Crown of Aragon
realms.note: Kept its own Cortes and fueros; dynastic union with Castile.

realms.name: Kingdom of Portugal
realms.note: Iberian Union since 1580 (Cortes of Tomar 1581): own institutions and empire (Brazil, Estado da India, Angola).

realms.name: Kingdom of Naples
realms.ruler: Philip III (viceroy Fernando Ruiz de Castro, Count of Lemos)

realms.name: Kingdom of Sicily
realms.ruler: Philip III (viceroy Bernardino de Cárdenas, Duke of Maqueda)

realms.name: Duchy of Milan
realms.ruler: Philip III (governor Juan Fernández de Velasco, Constable of Castile)
realms.note: Spanish since 1535; imperial fief.

realms.name: Habsburg Netherlands (the Archdukes)
realms.note: Ceded by Philip II in 1598; reverts to Spain if they die childless; Spanish army stays.

realms.name: United Provinces of the Netherlands
realms.ruler: States General; stadtholder Maurice of Nassau, Land's Advocate Johan van Oldenbarnevelt
realms.note: In revolt against Spain since 1568; Union of Utrecht 1579, Act of Abjuration 1581.

realms.name: Kingdom of England (and Ireland)
realms.note: Holds the Kingdom of Ireland (1542); Nine Years' War with Tyrone under way.

realms.name: O'Neill lordship of Tyrone
realms.note: Leading the Irish confederacy in the Nine Years' War (1593-1603).

realms.name: Kingdom of France
realms.note: Wars of Religion ended 1598 (Edict of Nantes, Peace of Vervins); Henri also King of (Lower) Navarre.

realms.name: Duchy of Savoy
realms.note: Dispute with France over Saluzzo (war in 1600).

realms.name: Republic of Genoa
realms.note: Aligned with Spain; holds Corsica.

realms.name: Republic of Venice
realms.note: Lost Cyprus 1571; keeps Crete, Ionian islands, Dalmatia.

realms.name: Grand Duchy of Tuscany
realms.note: Grand duchy since 1569; includes Pisa and Siena.

realms.name: Papal States
realms.note: Annexed Ferrara in 1598.

realms.name: Duchy of Modena and Reggio
realms.note: Este moved here after losing Ferrara 1598.

realms.name: Duchy of Parma and Piacenza
realms.note: Created 1545.

realms.name: Order of St John (Malta)
realms.note: Lost Rhodes 1522; Malta since 1530.

realms.name: Republic of Ragusa
realms.note: Ottoman tributary.

realms.name: Habsburg Austria (Archduchy)
realms.ruler: Emperor Rudolf II (Archduke Matthias governing Austria; Archduke Ferdinand in Inner Austria)
realms.note: Rudolf resides in Prague; Long Turkish War with the Ottomans since 1593.

realms.name: Holy Roman Empire
realms.note: Listed for the emperor's title; the realms below hold the land.

realms.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
realms.note: Habsburg crown land; Rudolf's residence.

realms.name: Royal Hungary
realms.note: Habsburg-held north and west of Hungary; the centre is Ottoman.

realms.name: Principality of Transylvania
realms.ruler: Michael the Brave (as Rudolf II's governor)
realms.note: Taken by Michael at Șelimbăr, Oct 1599; Báthory princes gone.

realms.name: Principality of Wallachia
realms.note: Broke with the Ottomans 1594; accepted Rudolf II's suzerainty 1598; takes Moldavia May 1600.

realms.name: Principality of Moldavia
realms.note: Polish protégé, still paying Ottoman tribute.

realms.name: Electorate of Saxony
realms.ruler: Christian II (regent Frederick William of Saxe-Weimar)

realms.name: Electorate of Cologne
realms.note: The city of Cologne itself is a free imperial city.

realms.name: Duchy of Pomerania (Stettin)
realms.note: Pomerania-Wolgast under Philip Julius.

realms.name: Free Imperial City of Lübeck
realms.note: The Hanse is in decline.

realms.name: Old Swiss Confederacy
realms.ruler: Federal Diet (Tagsatzung) of the Thirteen Cantons

realms.name: Denmark-Norway
realms.note: Norway ruled from Copenhagen since 1537; holds Gotland, Scania, Schleswig-Holstein shares.

realms.name: Kingdom of Sweden
realms.note: Riksdag deposed Sigismund III in July 1599; holds Estonia.

realms.name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth (Crown of Poland)
realms.note: Union of Lublin 1569; court moving to Warsaw since 1596; Livonia joint since 1561/1582.

realms.name: Grand Duchy of Lithuania
realms.note: Constituent of the Commonwealth (real union 1569).

realms.name: Duchy of Prussia
realms.ruler: Albert Frederick (administrator George Frederick of Brandenburg-Ansbach)
realms.note: Secularized Teutonic state, Polish fief since 1525.

realms.name: Duchy of Courland and Semigallia
realms.note: Polish-Lithuanian fief since 1561.

realms.name: Tsardom of Russia
realms.note: Holds Kazan, Astrakhan and western Siberia; Rurikids ended 1598.

realms.name: Nogai Horde
realms.note: Under growing Russian influence; Lesser Nogai west of the Volga under Crimea.

realms.name: Kazakh Khanate
realms.note: Took Tashkent region in the 1590s.

realms.name: Ottoman Empire
realms.note: At war with the Habsburgs (Long Turkish War); Celali revolts in Anatolia.

realms.name: Regency of Algiers
realms.note: Ottoman since 1518-29; Zayyanid Tlemcen absorbed 1554.

realms.name: Regency of Tunis
realms.note: Ottoman since 1574; deys rule from 1591.

realms.name: Zaydi Imamate of Yemen
realms.note: Revolt against Ottoman Yemen since 1597.

realms.name: Oman (Nabhani imamate interior)
realms.note: Coast (Muscat) held by Portugal.

realms.name: Kingdom of Hormuz
realms.note: Portuguese vassal since 1515.

realms.name: Safavid Iran
realms.note: Capital moved to Isfahan 1598; Herat and Mashhad retaken 1598; Tabriz still Ottoman.

realms.name: Kingdom of Kartli
realms.ruler: George X (Simon I captured by the Ottomans, 1599)

realms.name: Khanate of Bukhara
realms.ruler: Baqi Muhammad (Janid; father Jani Muhammad as nominal khan)
realms.note: Shaybanids ended 1598-99 after Abdullah Khan II.

realms.name: Khanate of Khwarazm (Khiva)
realms.note: Arabshahids restored after Bukharan occupation 1593-98.

realms.name: Yarkent Khanate
realms.note: Chagatayid successor of Moghulistan (1514); also holds Kashgar.

realms.name: Mughal Empire
realms.note: Akbar campaigning in the Deccan (Asirgarh, Ahmadnagar).

realms.name: Ahmadnagar Sultanate
realms.note: Under Mughal siege; city falls Aug 1600.

realms.name: Khandesh Sultanate
realms.note: Asirgarh falls to Akbar Jan 1601.

realms.name: Bijapur Sultanate
realms.note: Adil Shahi successor of the Bahmanis.

realms.name: Vijayanagara Empire (Aravidu)
realms.note: Rump state after Talikota 1565; Hampi abandoned.

realms.name: Madurai Nayaks
realms.note: Nominal Vijayanagara subordinate.

realms.name: Zamorin of Calicut
realms.note: Allied with the Portuguese against the Kunjali Marakkars (1599-1600).

realms.name: Jaffna Kingdom
realms.note: Portuguese tributary.

realms.name: Mewar
realms.note: Holding out against Akbar.

realms.name: Koch Bihar
realms.note: Allied to and dependent on the Mughals.

realms.name: Kantipur (Malla Nepal)
realms.note: Also holds Lalitpur.

realms.name: Phagmodrupa (Ü)
realms.note: Waning; Tsangpa rulers of Shigatse rising.

realms.name: Tsangpa dynasty
realms.note: Successor of Rinpungpa in Tsang (1565).

realms.name: Khalkha Mongols
realms.note: Nominally under the Chahar Great Khan.

realms.name: Jianzhou Jurchens
realms.note: Nominal Ming commandery; creating the Manchu script 1599.

realms.name: Ming dynasty
realms.note: After the Imjin War (ended 1598) and Bozhou revolt (1599-1600).

realms.name: Joseon
realms.note: Recovering from the Japanese invasions 1592-98.

realms.name: Japan (Toyotomi regime)
realms.ruler: Toyotomi Hideyori (minor) under the Five Elders led by Tokugawa Ieyasu; Emperor Go-Yōzei
realms.note: Hideyoshi died Sept 1598; Sekigahara Oct 1600.

realms.name: Tokugawa domain
realms.note: Largest daimyo, holding the Kanto since 1590.

realms.name: Ryukyu Kingdom
realms.note: Ming tributary; Satsuma invasion 1609.

realms.name: Đại Việt (Restored Lê)
realms.ruler: Lê Kính Tông (lord Trịnh Tùng governs)
realms.note: Nguyễn Hoàng governs the south (Thuận Hóa, Quảng Nam) in Lê name.

realms.name: Mạc remnant (Cao Bằng)
realms.note: Under Ming protection after losing Thăng Long 1592.

realms.name: Cambodia
realms.note: Lovek sacked by Ayutthaya 1594; Spanish-Portuguese adventurers killed 1599.

realms.name: Lan Na
realms.note: Burmese-installed prince; drifting to Ayutthaya (1602).

realms.name: Ayutthaya
realms.note: Independent from Burma since 1584; invading Lower Burma 1600.

realms.name: Ava (Restored Toungoo)
realms.note: Upper Burma after Toungoo collapse.

realms.name: Toungoo
realms.note: With Arakan took Pegu Dec 1599; Nanda Bayin killed.

realms.name: Arakan (Mrauk U)
realms.note: Holds Syriam (Thanlyin) after sacking Pegu.

realms.name: Johor Sultanate
realms.note: Successor of Malacca sultanate (1528).

realms.name: Mataram Sultanate
realms.note: Founded c.1586.

realms.name: Surabaya
realms.note: Leading East Javanese coastal power.

realms.name: Ternate Sultanate
realms.note: Expelled the Portuguese 1575.

realms.name: Tidore Sultanate
realms.note: Portuguese fort since 1578.

realms.name: Saadi Sultanate of Morocco
realms.note: Conquered Songhay 1591; Pashalik of Timbuktu.

realms.name: Songhay of Dendi
realms.note: Rump state after Tondibi 1591.

realms.name: Mali (rump)
realms.note: Failed attack on Djenné 1599.

realms.name: Bornu Sultanate
realms.ruler: Mai Idris Alooma or successor (chronology disputed)
realms.note: Holds Kanem after Alooma's campaigns.

realms.name: Kingdom of Kongo
realms.note: Christian kingdom; diocese 1596.

realms.name: Kingdom of Ndongo
realms.note: At war with Portuguese Angola (Luanda 1575).

realms.name: Ethiopian Empire
realms.note: Oromo migrations; Ottoman Habesh on the coast.

realms.name: Imamate of Aussa (Adal)
realms.note: Adal capital moved from Harar 1577.

realms.name: Funj Sultanate of Sennar
realms.note: Founded 1504.

realms.name: Kilwa Sultanate
realms.note: Sacked by the Zimba 1587; Portuguese-dominated coast.

realms.name: Mapuche (Araucanía)
realms.note: Destroying the Spanish towns south of the Biobío after Curalaba 1598.

realms.name: Itza kingdom
realms.note: Independent until 1697.

realms.name: Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg (Celle)
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Kingdom of Marwar
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Duchy of Mecklenburg
realms.ruler: Ulrich (Güstrow); Adolf Frederick I and John Albert II minors in Schwerin
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Kingdom of Navarre (Lower Navarre and Béarn)
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Personal union with France; merged 1620.

realms.name: Kingdom of Ireland
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. Kingdom since 1542 under the English crown; Gaelic lords under Tyrone in revolt (Nine Years' War).

realms.name: Republic of Lucca
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

realms.name: Ajuran
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised. In decline.

realms.name: Mossi kingdoms
realms.note: Still standing; carried forward when realm ids were harmonised.

dublin.note: Kingdom of Ireland under the English crown (Lord Deputy); Nine Years' War.

barcelona.note: Crown of Aragon under the Spanish king.

riga.note: Duchy of Livonia, held jointly by Poland and Lithuania; Swedish attack 1600-01.

kyiv.note: Transferred to the Crown of Poland 1569.

sarai.note: Lower Volga steppe: Russian forts (Tsaritsyn 1589) but Nogai pastures.

buda.note: Budin eyalet; under Habsburg siege attempts in the Long Turkish War.

tbilisi.note: Ottoman garrison since 1578; Kartli princes contest the area.

gaur.note: Bengal Subah; Bara-Bhuyan chiefs resist in the east.

vijayanagara.note: Hampi ruined after 1565; local nayaks between Bijapur and the Aravidu rump.

lhasa.note: Ü under fading Phagmodrupa; Tsangpa expanding.

hakata.note: Chikuzen: Kobayakawa Hideaki's restored fief or Toyotomi direct land.

vijaya.note: Quảng Nam, governed by the Nguyễn in the Lê name.

pegu.note: Sacked Dec 1599 by Toungoo and Arakan; largely abandoned.

trowulan.note: East Java between Surabaya and other princes; Mataram not yet there.

great_zimbabwe.note: Abandoned site; Karanga chiefdoms between Torwa and Mutapa.

quebec.note: Innu/Montagnais land; Tadoussac post only from mid-1600.

new_orleans.note: Chitimacha and other chiefdoms; no state.

events.name: Ismail I founds the Safavid state
Ottoman conquest of the Mamluk Sultanate
First Battle of Panipat: Babur founds the Mughal Empire
Battle of Wayna Daga ends Adal's conquest of Ethiopia
Peace of Cateau-Cambrésis ends the Italian Wars
Fall of Vilcabamba, last Inca state
Hideyoshi completes unification of Japan at Odawara
Battle of Tondibi: Morocco defeats Songhay
Rurikids end; Boris Godunov tsar (Time of Troubles era)
Edict of Nantes ends the French Wars of Religion
Michael the Brave takes Transylvania at Șelimbăr
Toungoo and Arakan sack Pegu; Nanda Bayin's fall

sources: Geoffrey Parker, The Grand Strategy of Philip II (1998) and Europe in Crisis 1598-1648
John F. Richards, The Mughal Empire (New Cambridge History of India)
Roger Savory, Iran under the Safavids
Frederick Mote and Denis Twitchett (eds), Cambridge History of China vol. 7 (Ming)
Yuri Bregel, An Historical Atlas of Central Asia
open_questions: How to model the Spanish composite monarchy: Aragon, Portugal, Naples, Sicily, Milan and the Archdukes' Netherlands are listed as separate realms with overlord castile (personal union), while American and Philippine holdings are held by castile directly.
Wallachia's overlord: Michael the Brave recognized Rudolf II (1598) while Ottoman suzerainty was disputed; recorded as austria.
Tbilisi: Ottoman garrison (since 1578, confirmed 1590) versus Kartli control in 1599-1600 is uncertain.
Pegu on 1 Jan 1600: sacked and burned by Toungoo and Arakan in Dec 1599; who governed the ruins is unclear.
Hakata (Chikuzen): Kobayakawa Hideaki's fief or Toyotomi direct land in late 1599.
Bornu: Idris Alooma's reign is dated 1564-1596 or 1571-1603; the ruler in 1600 is disputed.
Bukhara: the Janid succession (Jani Muhammad, Baqi Muhammad) in 1599-1601 is variously dated.
Cambodian kingship in 1599-1600 is disputed in the chronicles.
Great Zimbabwe, Trowulan, Lhasa and Hampi lie in areas with no clear governing state; holders are best guesses.
Resolved in the id harmonisation: the ended list is recomputed against 1500.json (astrakhan_khanate is astrakhan; sibir_khanate dropped as never listed).
Kyoto/Japan holder 'japan' stands for the Toyotomi regency; Tokugawa Ieyasu was the de facto leader from Osaka Castle.

Id harmonisation: the Habsburg Netherlands of the Archdukes use burgundy (continuation of the Burgundian Netherlands), the United Provinces use netherlands (the same state as the 1815 kingdom), the Zaydi imamate uses yemen, Phagmodrupa uses tibet, Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel uses brunswick and the Regency of Tunis keeps tunis (Hafsid Tunis continued as an Ottoman regency, so neither formed nor ended).

The id ireland follows the island's polity: Gaelic lordships to 1500, the Kingdom of Ireland under the English crown from 1542 (added here); Tyrone is first_listed, not formed. Norway is counted as ended in 1536 (Danish province) and formed again in 1814; the Albertine duchy as merged when it took the Saxon electorate (1547).

Added as still standing: Brunswick-Lüneburg, Marwar, Mecklenburg, Navarre (personal union with France until 1620), Ireland, Lucca, Ajuran, Mossi. The Jolof empire is counted as ended at its break-up (1549); the rump kingdom of Jolof is not tracked.
